title: Harden repository audit achieved-completion evidence
summary: Make strict repository-audit completion distinguish achieved, blocked, and other incomplete rows in CLI evidence, and exhaustively lock category/status, semantic-obligation, and risky-registry behavior with isolated end-to-end tests.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W11-001, AUDIT-FIND-W11-002, and AUDIT-FIND-W11-003, while independently revalidating resolved-in-audit AUDIT-FIND-W11-004. The audit tool already contained most semantic enforcement, but strict CLI output did not report blocked-row counts and the required exhaustive compatibility, multi-flag, registry-glob, and CLI round-trip regressions were absent.
behavior_before: Strict --check --require-complete rejected blocked and pending rows individually but did not emit aggregate achieved/blocked/incomplete counts. Tests sampled only one incompatible status, one blocked category, and a few registry paths, and did not drive the complete write/merge/check CLI sequence against an isolated repository.
behavior_after: Strict CLI checks always report achieved, blocked, and other-incomplete counts before their result. A hidden --root seam routes every CLI action through an explicitly selected repository for safe isolated testing. The suite checks blocked completion for every category, the full category/achieved-status cross-product, generated/archive/runtime plus binary multi-flag obligations, every high/critical registry glob case-insensitively, mixed achieved/pending/blocked CLI output, and actual isolated --write/--merge-reviews/--merge-findings/--merge-errors/--check --require-complete transitions.
tests_added: Blocked rows fail achieved completion for every allowed file category.
Every allowed category is checked against every achieved status, including metadata_verified compatibility.
Every high/critical risky-file registry glob maps to high risk case-insensitively.
Generated-binary, archived-binary, and runtime-binary rows must verify every distinct obligation.
Strict CLI output reports achieved, blocked, and other incomplete counts for a mixed isolated matrix.
The isolated Git-repository round trip drives CLI write, review/finding/error merge, successful strict check, and blocked strict failure.
manual_validation: Adjacent audit-check plus repository-audit ledger suites passed: 46 tests and 135 subtests.
Canonical risky-file registry validation, targeted git diff --check, and strict worktree coverage passed with 1,168 valid packets.
Focused repository-audit ledger suite passed: 37 tests and 135 subtests.

Full packaged release self-test was run with required tests. Environment, Tauri prerequisites, package policy, tool integration, and end-to-end smoke passed; the gate remained red only on accumulated unrelated generated-inventory/summary drift, missing packaged active-doc targets, the known package cycle, two unrelated Ruff B023 findings, and the current WebView static-assets assertion.
Packet-local suites, generated checks, and strict worktree coverage passed; full release gate completed with documented unrelated baseline failures.
Targeted Ruff validation passed for implementation and tests.
Targeted summary refresh wrote three current summaries; project-index/dependency-graph and feature-map check modes passed.
rollback_plan: Revert the strict CLI count reporting, the hidden isolated-root test seam, the focused tests, generated summaries/maps, and this packet together. The default repository root and all audit evidence formats remain unchanged.
notes: Tooling-only audit-integrity change; no media, runtime, source-library, or immutable audit-ledger artifacts are touched. The first focused run produced four subtest failures because the new line_reviewed_with_findings fixtures omitted their independently required finding IDs; the fixture was corrected without weakening production validation, after which all focused and adjacent tests passed. AUDIT-FIND-W11-004 was already marked resolved-in-audit; this packet adds exhaustive current-registry verification without modifying the registry. The first release-build wrapper attempt was rejected before execution because its verified temporary destination had been pre-created; the corrected build ran, but its ten-minute outer wrapper timed out while the owned package verifier continued. The verifier completed, and the package test was rerun directly with a longer bound to capture its exact unrelated failure set. The exact temporary package tree was then removed.
